turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Follower count stopped predicting reach. When did this actually happen and on which platforms?

turns.speaker: expert
turns.text: Every major platform, LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, X, now uses AI to determine who sees what based on individual relevance rather than follower relationship or chronology. A post from three days ago can outperform one from three hours ago if the algorithm judges it more relevant to a specific viewer. Growing a following is necessary. It's no longer sufficient.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The engagement rate formula most marketers still use is apparently wrong. What's the problem?

turns.speaker: expert
turns.text: Engagement rate by follower count, the 2015-era formula, is close to meaningless on algorithm-driven platforms because follower count has almost no relationship to distribution anymore. Use engagement rate by reach for organic reporting, and engagement rate by impressions for paid. The exception is LinkedIn, where the follower graph still genuinely drives distribution.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: LinkedIn carousels have a 21.77% median engagement rate. That's the highest of any format on any major platform?

turns.speaker: expert
turns.text: That's the figure. LinkedIn sits at 5.20% average overall, but carousels pull well above that at 21.77% median. Instagram carousels also significantly outperform Reels: 6.90% versus Reels at 3.31%, against an overall Instagram average of just 0.48%.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: TikTok's completion rate on sub-30-second content is 72%. What does that tell you about how the algorithm works?

turns.speaker: expert
turns.text: Watch time and completion rate are the primary quality signals, above raw view count. Short, high-retention content consistently beats longer content with high drop-off across TikTok, Reels, and Shorts. The hook in the first three seconds is doing algorithmic work before it does any narrative work: it proves to the distribution system that the content is worth showing more people.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: 87% of marketers used generative AI in Q1 2026, up from 51% two years prior. What does that mean for organic performance?

turns.speaker: expert
turns.text: Generic AI-assisted content is now the baseline everyone has, not a differentiator. On a platform flooded with it, the specific first-hand detail is what actually separates a post from the noise. The brands winning with AI are using it to remove production bottlenecks, not to replace the editorial judgment about what's worth making.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Why do saves and qualified traffic matter more than likes?

turns.speaker: expert
turns.text: Raw engagement, likes and views, is becoming less predictive every quarter because platforms got too good at generating lightweight, low-friction interaction. What's actually predictive now sits further down: saves, qualified traffic, assisted conversions, lead quality. A lower engagement number tied to genuine intent is often worth more than a higher one driven by broad, low-commitment entertainment reach.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Threads gets a 42% engagement lift from responsiveness. That's higher than any other platform tracked?

turns.speaker: expert
turns.text: Yes, 42% is the highest lift from comment reply engagement of any platform tracked, compared to roughly 30% on LinkedIn and 21% on Instagram. It's also one of the highest-leverage, lowest-cost actions available. Most teams still treat replying to comments as an afterthought rather than a standing workflow habit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Social SEO, the idea that TikTok and Instagram are search engines now. Is that actually playing out?

turns.speaker: expert
turns.text: Users are typing full questions directly into TikTok and Instagram search bars rather than starting on Google. Both platforms scan captions, on-screen text, and spoken audio transcripts for keyword relevance. Saying a keyword out loud in the first three seconds of a video measurably improves search ranking within the platform.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does the zero-click penalty mean for brands that built social as a funnel to their website?

turns.speaker: expert
turns.text: Posts with outbound links are consistently deprioritized because platforms optimize for in-app time. A genuinely useful carousel or a complete answer in the caption now outperforms content built primarily as a funnel to a landing page. Social is increasingly a destination for top and middle of funnel content, not a pipe to somewhere else.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Early engagement velocity, the first 30 to 60 minutes, triggers wider distribution. How should that change posting workflows?

turns.speaker: expert
turns.text: Content earning comments, saves, and shares within the first 30 to 60 minutes gets pushed to a significantly wider audience. The algorithm reads early engagement as a quality signal and amplifies accordingly. Posting when your actual audience is live matters more in 2026 than it did when reach was closer to proportional to follower count.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: UK active social posting rates fell from 61% to 49% since 2024. What's driving that?

turns.speaker: expert
turns.text: Roughly two-thirds of US teens now use an AI chatbot at least sometimes for things social media used to provide. Social platforms are increasingly competing with AI interfaces for raw discretionary attention. The drop reflects a broader shift where passive consumption continues but active participation is declining.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What's the most common mistake brands make with AI content and social in 2026?

turns.speaker: expert
turns.text: Using AI for production speed and skipping the editorial judgment about what's worth making and why. The AI produces roughly the first half of the work. The differentiated, trust-earning half is still a human editorial call. On a platform flooded with AI-assisted content that mostly looks the same, the specific first-hand detail is the only differentiator.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How many KPIs should a campaign actually track?

turns.speaker: expert
turns.text: Three to five primary KPIs tied to an actual business goal. For a growth goal: reach, engagement rate by reach, follower growth rate. For a revenue goal: CTR, conversion rate, social ROI. One primary KPI is genuinely enough. A 40-metric dashboard is not a strategy, and never benchmark across platforms: a 0.5% engagement rate is healthy on Instagram and a warning sign on TikTok.
